messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: head's up: merging bbvb into develop
parts:
[moved to stan-dev]

I'm not exactly sure what "outputting stuff" means. Is
it a Stan or CmdStan issue? Anyway, if there's an issue,
we obviously can't release it until it's fixed, which means
waiting for 2.8.

In any case, there needs to be a unit test that catches the
problem or it's going to get released in a broken state. We do
not do any by-hand testing on releases, nor do we want to. If this
kind of thing can happen, then it signals we don't yet have an
appropriate set of tests for advi.

- Bob

P.S. I'm bcc-ing Kui and Dustin, but if they want to communicate to
Stan developers about release issues, they should also be on stan-dev.

P.P.S. As I've said before, I think the name "advi" is misleading
because the key point isn't autodiff --- any method of computing
model gradients would work. But I can live with it that's the
majority feeling or if it's too much of a pain to change.

What's the name of the CmdStan top-level equivalent of "sample" and
"optimize" and "diagnose" for advi?


> On Jun 23, 2015, at 2:45 PM, Alp Kucukelbir <akucu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> hi daniel, bob + dustin, kui,
>
> dustin told me that you guys are considering

> news. so happy.

> i just wanted to alert everyone to this. i'm sure

>
> cheers
> alp

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] head's up: merging bbvb into develop
parts:
I’m not sure what that means either. I can add a test to see if variational inference prints anything to standard output (which may be what Kui means?).

The name of the CmdStan top-level equivalent is currently `experimental variational`, e.g., `./bernoulli experimental variational data file=bernoulli.data.R`. It is under `experimental` at the moment because I believe EP was supposed to be (or is) as well.

I tend to agree on the comments about the ADVI name. It’s nice that it emphasizes one of the primary features that distinguishes our variational inference from other implementations. However, there are other primary features in place too, e.g., parameter transformations, and there will be many other excellent features in the future such as my long term goal of putting in copulas to generally learn the dependency structure among the latent variables. I personally like “automatic variational inference”, as in the title of the preprint and which follows the motivation of probabilistic programming more closely. Regardless, Alp has been spearheading the project from the get-go, and I’m happy to stick by whatever he decides to name it.

Dustin

You’ve hit one of my sore spots — the terrible pollution of names (really, branding)
endemic to machine learning and increasingly statistics. Honestly, I don’t think we
should let that terrible behavior affect out naming choices as most of our users are
not in the machine learning community (and if we were really serious about it
we’d have to start following startups and use misspellings).

Following the other algorithms we should just call the base folder “vb" and then
have this specific implementation in that folder with a given name. Perhaps
“unconstrained_gauss_vb” or the like.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: head's up: merging bbvb into develop
parts:
Thanks for reposting on stan-dev.

The first order of business is to create an issue. Ideally
this will come with a test that fails. Feel free to actually
write it as a test in a branch and then we can work on the fix
in that branch.

We do not want any fixes that do not come with unit tests
that (a) fail in the old version, and (b) pass in the new.

I don't even know if this is a CmdStan or Stan issue right
now given the fluid nature of the command code recently.

Nothing should be testing cin or cout, but should instead
use passed-in stringstreams to collect answers.

Daniel will hopefully know how to fix the problem.

And by the way, this is why we like those completely broken
tests that just make sure output's getting through. (They're
broken because they're typically hardwired to exact output rather
than more functional.)

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] head's up: merging bbvb into develop
parts:
> On Jun 24, 2015, at 11:27 AM, Alp Kucukelbir <akucu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> adding experimental was something you guys asked me to do!

Sorry about the miscommunication --- if someone asked you
to make it part of the command name, I missed it, or I would've
objected then.

We just wanted to label the whole algorithm "experimental" in
the manual and perhaps spit out a warning at the top of running
it to reinforce the idea. Then we could easily remove those things
later without breaking backward compatiblity. That's how we rolled
out the optimizer.

> i vote for "vi" or just "variational".
>
> i just think the documentation etc. should refer to the algorithm
> as ADVI. just like how cmdStan uses "sample" but refers to
> "NUTS" in the manual.

CmdStan uses "engine=nuts" (if I recall the syntax correctly)
by default for "sample". So So VI could use "engine=advi" or
whatever by default to leave room for future implementations
in the same command.

Michael may have some input here having designed that hierarchical
command structure in the first place. It'll get flattened
out considerably into its own command in RStan and PyStan.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] head's up: merging bbvb into develop
parts:
> On Jun 24, 2015, at 3:00 PM, Alp Kucukelbir <akucu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ok. dustin fixed the lack of output business. it seems
> like the definition of "write_iteration" changed.

Glad to hear it. Once things are merged, then it's on
whoever changes things to make sure unit tests all pass,
which is another reason to have good tests. And a good
reason to merge early and often, which wasn't really possible
with this major-new-feature project.

> i'll get rid of the "experimental" keyword and update
> all the documentation etc.
>
> i don't mind us changing the interface down the road.

I do mind changing interfaces. Breaking backward compatibility
is a huge deal in non-research code, because it breaks things
users have developed and forces them to learn new idioms. And
they're not invested in the guts of our package as we are, so for
them, it's just a huge hassle when they update the package
and everything breaks.

- Bob

is up to date with stan/develop, and it works great with cmdStan/develop.

cheers
alp

parts:
As an FYI, the pull request for feature/advi-command is still outstanding: https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstan/pull/117. It's required to run variational inference in cmdstan.

Now that feature/bbvb is merged, hopefully someone is also interested in adding variational inference to the other interfaces.

Dustin
